For Vermont specifically, the book argues that Domain 2 (Data and Technology) is the binding constraint, while the Blueprint's patient-centered medical homes and Community Health Teams give Domain 3 (care delivery) a long head start. The gap is not clinical capability;

Blueprint-participating PCMH practices with active Community Health Team support score 40-60% on the care-delivery readiness domain -- strong by national standards. Most Vermont hospitals score only 25-45% on the data-and-technology domain. Before assuming downside risk, close the second gap, not the first -- it is already closed.
Vermont's Blueprint practices and Community Health Teams give it a head start on care delivery; data and technology is the weaker domain. Before assuming downside risk, close that gap first.

Vermont's own readiness data makes the point concretely: most Vermont hospitals score only 25-45% on the Data and Technology domain of the VBC Transformation Readiness Assessment -- the domain covering attribution list generation and total cost of care measurement.
The Data and Technology domain of the VBC Readiness Assessment covers exactly this: attribution list generation and total cost of care measurement.
